title: Searching and Sorting: A Three-Lesson Course
purpose: Multi-lesson fixture for course/module/lesson hierarchy, prerequisite continuity, cross-lesson vocabulary and visual consistency, cumulative assessment, and partial lesson regeneration.

learner.audience: Beginning computer-science learners progressing from search to sorting trade-offs.

objectives.statement: Explain why sorted order enables binary search and trace one lookup.
Choose search/sort strategies from data state and number of queries.
criteria: Compares one lookup with repeated lookups

sources.title: Searching and sorting: three-lesson course note
sources.creator: Alystria fixture authors

claims.statement: Sorted order lets a binary-search comparison rule out one side of the candidate interval.
Insertion sort maintains a sorted prefix by shifting larger prefix items before inserting the next item.
Sorting once can benefit many later searches, while sorting for one lookup may cost more than a linear scan.

scenes.title: Course concept thread
scenes.narration: The course connects ordered data, maintaining order, and choosing when preprocessing pays off.
scenes.visualIntent: A persistent three-lesson concept thread marks prerequisite edges and current location.
scenes.captionText: Ordered data → maintain order → choose by workload
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A three-node prerequisite graph lists each lesson and its required prior objectives.

scenes.title: Lesson 1: binary search
scenes.narration: Sorted order turns each comparison into a safe elimination of one side.
scenes.visualIntent: A short array trace uses the same index typography and color-independent markers used throughout the course.
scenes.captionText: Sorted order makes side elimination valid
scenes.accessibilityDescription: An array trace identifies the remaining candidate interval after each comparison.

scenes.title: Lesson 2: insertion sort
scenes.narration: Insertion sort grows a sorted prefix. It shifts larger items right, then inserts the next value into the gap.
scenes.visualIntent: A variable-state table marks sorted prefix, key, shifts, and insertion using the lesson-one visual vocabulary.
scenes.captionText: Maintain a sorted prefix: shift, then insert
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A four-step table narrates the prefix, selected key, shifts, and final insertion.

scenes.title: Lesson 3: choose by workload
scenes.narration: For one lookup, a linear scan may be enough. For many lookups, sorting once can make later binary searches worthwhile. Context decides.
scenes.visualIntent: A scenario matrix compares existing order, input size, number of queries, mutation, memory, and risk.
scenes.captionText: No algorithm is always best—choose for the workload
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A text-first decision matrix compares one lookup and many-lookups scenarios.

scenes.title: Cumulative practice
scenes.narration: Choose an approach for three data workloads, then justify each choice using order, query count, and update cost.
scenes.visualIntent: Three untimed scenario cards preserve keyboard navigation and show feedback tied to objectives.
scenes.captionText: Choose and justify using data state and workload
scenes.accessibilityDescription: Three scenario prompts each provide labeled choices and text feedback.

qualityAssertions.description: No lesson depends on an objective introduced later in the course.
Index, value, current state, and prerequisite visual tokens remain consistent across lessons.
Candidate interval and sorted prefix retain one definition throughout.
Editing lesson two narration preserves lesson one rendered artifacts byte-for-byte while invalidating cumulative review.
Cumulative practice traces feedback to all three objectives.

provenance.notes: The course note and every scenario are locally authored for deterministic cross-lesson tests.
